description: The figure is a two-level donut (sunburst-style) pie chart showing how the MMAR benchmark is distributed across high-level layers and their associated task categories. The inner ring contains 4 slices: Semantic Layer (41.2%, medium blue), Perception (percentage not clearly readable due to an overlaid gray box, dark blue), Cultural Layer (14.1%, light gray), and Signal Layer (4.3%, darker slate-blue). The outer ring breaks these into 14 labeled categories: for the Semantic Layer, Content Analysis (largest outer slice, light blue), Emotion & Intention (small, light blue), and Speaker Analysis (small-to-medium, light blue); for Perception, Environmental Perception & Reasoning (large, blue), Counting & Statistics (medium, blue), Music Theory (medium, blue), Correlation Analysis (small-to-medium, blue), Temporal Analysis (small, blue), and Spatial Analysis (small, blue); for the Cultural Layer, Professional Knowledge & Reasoning (medium, gray), Culture of Speaker (small, gray), Imagination (small, gray), and Aesthetic Analysis (small, gray); and for the Signal Layer, Acoustic Quality Analysis (very small, slate-blue), Anomaly Detection (very small, slate-blue), and Audio Difference Analysis (very small, slate-blue). There is no separate legend; labels are placed directly on slices, with only the inner-ring slices showing explicit percentages, and no slices appear exploded or offset; visually, the largest segments (e.g., Content Analysis and Environmental Perception & Reasoning) occupy the widest arcs.
